territorial_scope.description: Applies to sales and leases in Utah, whose Sales and Use Tax Act contains the exemption.

evidence.quote: amounts paid or charged for a purchase or lease made by a qualifying data center or an occupant of a qualifying data center

summary.short: Utah Code 59-12-104 lists sales and use tax exemptions. Item (84) exempts purchases or leases of machinery, equipment and repair parts by a qualifying data center or its occupant, when used in its operation and with an economic life of one or more years. Effective 7/1/2026, superseded 1/1/2027.
summary.long: Utah Code 59-12-104 is the exemptions section of the Sales and Use Tax Act (Chapter 12). Exemptions from the taxes imposed by the chapter are listed in numbered items (1) to (103), covering, among others, government purchases, vending, airline in-flight sales, farming, prescription and medical items, manufacturing, mining and refining equipment, semiconductor materials, industrial energy, school and fundraising sales, and disaster-related imports. Item (84) exempts amounts paid or charged for a purchase or lease, by a qualifying data center or an occupant of a qualifying data center, of machinery, equipment, or normal operating repair or replacement parts that are used in the operation of the data center or the occupant's operations there and have an economic life of one or more years. The excerpt does not define qualifying data center. The header states the text is effective 7/1/2026 and superseded 1/1/2027, and the text notes it was amended by Chapter 433, 2026 General Session. The excerpt contains no enforcement provisions and no thresholds for item (84) beyond the economic-life test.

notes: Registry title says the data-center exemption covers new or expanding data centers, but subsection (84) covers any qualifying data center and its occupants; 'qualifying data center' is not defined in this section. Subsection (84) states no sunset date, whereas subsections (55), (56), (57) and (62) end on June 30, 2027. Header metadata says effective 7/1/2026 and superseded 1/1/2027; neither date appears in the section body. The amendment history cites only Chapter 433, 2026 General Session, and the text carries no markings showing which provisions that chapter changed. Subsection (84) is the only data-center provision in the text.
